front.title: PQC Agility for WIMSE Workload Identity
front.workgroup: Workload Identity in Multi System Environments

abstract.t: This document defines PQC algorithm agility requirements and migration mechanisms for the WIMSE (Workload Identity in Multi System Environments) framework. It specifies how workload identity tokens, SVID certificates, and trust bundles transition from classical to ML-DSA and hybrid composite algorithms, with epoch-aware rotation coordinated by the Sanctum rotation orchestration framework.
This revision (-03) adds normative requirements for hybrid SVID certificates, epoch-signaling in SPIFFE trust bundles, and alignment with draft-vicente-pquip-pqc-rotation-orchestration.

note.title: IPR Considerations
note.t: U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 64/080,137 (2026-06-01) and U.S. Patent Application No. 19/698,870 (2026-06-05). Sanctum SecOps PEN root: 1.3.6.1.4.1.65953.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Workload identity systems (SPIFFE, SPIRE, and WIMSE-compliant implementations) issue short-lived X.509 SVIDs and JWT-SVIDs to authenticate workloads in cloud-native environments. As these environments migrate to PQC, every issued credential must carry a PQC or hybrid composite signature, and trust bundles must reflect current PQC signing key epochs. This document defines the algorithm agility profile and orchestration requirements for PQC migration in WIMSE deployments.

dl.dd: SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document. An X.509 certificate or JWT carrying a SPIFFE ID as a Subject Alternative Name.
The set of CA certificates and signing keys trusted by a SPIFFE trust domain.
An SVID signed with an ML-DSA or hybrid composite key as defined in this document.

section.name: PQC-SVID Requirements
section.t: WIMSE deployments conformant with this profile MUST issue X.509 SVIDs signed with ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87. Hybrid composite SVIDs (ML-DSA + ECDSA P-256) SHOULD be issued during the transition period for backward compatibility with relying parties that cannot yet validate ML-DSA signatures. The PQCHC extension (draft-vicente-lamps-pqchc) MUST be included in PQC-SVIDs to bind the ML-DSA and classical key components.
JWT-SVIDs in PQC-capable WIMSE deployments MUST use the ML-DSA algorithm identifier in the JOSE header. The epoch_id MUST be included as a private claim (pqc_epoch_id) in the JWT payload.

section.name: Trust Bundle Epoch Signaling
section.t: SPIFFE trust bundles extended for PQC deployments MUST include an epoch_id field at the trust domain level. The trust bundle refresh endpoint MUST return the current epoch_id and MUST include both the current and previous epoch's signing certificates during the grace period following epoch rotation. Trust bundle consumers MUST reject bundles where the included epoch_id is lower than the highest previously accepted epoch_id for that trust domain.

section.name: Integration with Rotation Orchestration
section.t: WIMSE Signing Authorities participating in orchestrated PQC rotation (draft-vicente-pquip-pqc-rotation-orchestration) MUST register as protocol stacks with the Rotation Orchestrator. The Signing Authority MUST emit an epoch readiness signal when its trust bundle has been updated with the new epoch's certificate and all in-flight SVID issuance operations have completed. SVID issuance MUST be paused during the COMMIT state of the orchestration state machine.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: PQC-SVIDs provide HNDL resistance for workload-to-workload authentication. The epoch_id claim in JWT-SVIDs prevents replay of credentials issued under a compromised prior epoch. Trust bundle consumers MUST implement the epoch monotonicity check to prevent epoch-rollback attacks. WIMSE Signing Authorities MUST use HSM-backed ML-DSA signing keys where deployment environment permits.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to register the pqc_epoch_id JWT claim name in the IANA JSON Web Token Claims registry.
